newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes weaker on interest rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes weaker on interest rate cut.

text.p: * Peso hits a low of 26.305 to dollar
The Philippine peso closed at 26.304 to the dollar, lower than Monday's close of 26.287, as arbitrage money flowed out of the system due to the softening of domestic interest rates, traders said.
Short-term interest rates went down after the Central Bank cut its benchmark overnight borrowing rate earlier in the day by 25 basis points to 10.75 percent.
Longer-termed Treasury bill rates were also lower after fresh money was released last Friday following the one percentage point cut in banks' reserve requirements.
"When interest rates go down, fund managers tend to go out of the system. It's a knee-jerk reaction," one trader said.
The withdrawal of arbitrage money created a demand for dollars which pushed the peso value down to as low as 26.305 by late session.
However, the peso rebounded slightly as some banks decided to take profit and sold their dollar holdings at above 26.300.
"Some banks were still long on dollars," another trader said, citing the huge inflow they received from overseas workers during the Christmas season.
The Central Bank was on the sidelines, posting its selling rate at 26.310 and buying rate at 26.295 and later at 26.298.
Traders said they expected the peso to weaken further in the coming days as more orders come in from foreign fund managers to convert their investments back to dollars.
